prerequisites: Knowledge of Graphic Expression at the level of Technical Drawing subjects from high school and the Graphic Expression and Assisted Design course from the first year.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and abilities to apply graphic engineering techniques.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds upon general secondary education, typically found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes aspects involving knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students can apply their knowledge to their work or vocation professionally and possess the competencies typically demonstrated through the formulation and defense of arguments and problem-solving within their field of study.
Students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their field of study) to make judgments that include reflection on relevant social, scientific, or ethical issues.
Students have developed the learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding, and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, abilities, and skills in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Ability to manage specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Ability to analyze and assess the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Ability to apply quality principles and methods.

assessment_rules: To pass the course, a final grade of 5/10 or higher is required. Students must achieve a minimum of 4/10 in the Presential Exam and 5/10 in the Distance Assessment Project (EED). For the ordinary June call, the final grade is calculated as 80% Presential Exam + 10% Continuous Assessment Tests (5% each) + 10% Distance Assessment Project. For extraordinary calls in September or December, the final grade is 90% Presential Exam + 10% Distance Assessment Project, with continuous assessment grades not being considered. Both the Presential Exam and EED are compulsory; failure to submit or attend either results in a 'not presented' grade.
